text:
olga: quick QA catch — ruby SDK retry backoff looks different from python/go. on transient 502s our ruby client retries every 500ms fixed while python uses exponential. causes thundering reties on warmups.

ben: huh, did we intentionally make ruby fixed? I thought parity was exponential with jitter.

drew: code snippet from lib/redwood/retry.rb shows: `sleep(RETRY_INTERVAL) # 0.5s` not exponential. probably a carryover from initial minimal impl.

samira: that explains why some onboarding sampleapps spike in logs when the endpoint is under short load. users report many small bursts.

olga: reproduction: run sampleapp-rb with local mock that returns 502 for first 2 attempts, we see 4 immediate retries spaced 500ms then success, whereas python spreads them 100ms, 200ms, 400ms.

ben: proposed fix: change Ruby backoff to exponential with cap and jitter to match other SDKs. e.g. base=0.1, factor=2, cap=2. add small jitter +-20%.

drew: will open tiny PR to swap retry implementation and add unit parity tests against python golden timings.

ci-bot: PR #711 opened by drew: feat/rb-retry-exponential-parity (checks: lint, unit, integration).

ci-bot: integration failed: `retry-timing-test` mismatch due to non-deterministic jitter.

samira: test should assert backoff bounds instead of exact times. also seed RNG in test for deterministic jitter.

drew: updated tests to check within min/max window and seeded jitter. re-run.

ci-bot: all checks passed.

ben: can we add a short note in changelog and bump minor version? also update quickstart README so sampleapp mentions retry behavior and how to configure backoff.

olga: please also run smoke against go sdk to confirm parity. drew, can you add cross-lang e2e?

drew: adding a smoke that instruments timings across python/go/rb in harness. will follow up in a separate PR.

samira: thanks — this should reduce onboarding noise for customers hitting transient infra errors. closing after changelog + release PR. :thumbsup:
